statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-14676 is a heap buffer overflow in the pg_stat_statements contrib module's query normalization, reachable through crafted queries containing array constants, that lets the query author run arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database. PostgreSQL's advisory, https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14676/, lists only major version 18 as affected (fixed in 18.6) and states that versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected. The fix, commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/8a31ffc2d4cc5e2f3fb42b6a41b7db802716615d on the REL_18_STABLE branch, replaces the fixed-size output buffer in generate_normalized_query() with a growable one; the fixed-size buffer did not allow for the " /*, ... */" comment that constant-list squashing appends after a squashed list. List squashing was added in PostgreSQL 18 by commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/62d712ecfd940f60e68bde5b6972b6859937c412, and neither commit is in the REL_16_STABLE branch. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are PostgreSQL 16: the server binary /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres in 16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0, on both x86_64 and aarch64, reports 16.13, 16.14, 16.15 and 16.16. We checked /usr/lib/postgresql16/pg_stat_statements.so in every published postgresql16-contrib package for Alpine 3.23 (16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0, x86_64 and aarch64, checksums verified against the package index): none contains the "/*, ... */" squashing string, while each contains the module's own pg_stat_statements_reset name. As a positive control, the same search finds the string in pg_stat_statements.so from the DHI postgresql18-contrib 18.7-r0 package for Alpine 3.23 on both architectures. Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-14676 under its 16.15-r0 secfixes with the rest of that release's advisories, but the PostgreSQL 16 code never contained the vulnerable squashing path. The vulnerable code is not present in this owner.

PostgreSQL states that versions before 18 are not affected by CVE-2026-14676 (pg_stat_statements heap buffer overflow via crafted queries containing array constants): https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14676/ lists only major version 18. The fix, https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/8a31ffc2d4cc5e2f3fb42b6a41b7db802716615d, corrects the normalized-query buffer size for squashed constant lists, code introduced by commit 62d712ecfd940f60e68bde5b6972b6859937c412 ("Introduce squashing of constant lists in query jumbling"), which is in PostgreSQL 18 and not on the REL_17_STABLE branch; the fix was back-patched to 18 only. pg_stat_statements.so is shipped in postgresql17-contrib, but every published DHI postgresql17 build for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0) is PostgreSQL 17, as its postgres server binary reports on both x86_64 and aarch64, so it does not contain the list-squashing code. Alpine lists this CVE under the postgresql17 17.11-r0 secfixes, but PostgreSQL 17.11 made no change for it.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-14676 (PostgreSQL pg_stat_statements heap buffer overflow executes arbitrary code): the query author can write past a buffer in pg_stat_statements with crafted queries containing array constants. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14676/ says only major version 18 is affected and lists 18.6 as its fixed release, and the 18.6 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.6/, list this CVE. The fix on the REL_18_STABLE branch is https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/8a31ffc2d4cc5e2f3fb42b6a41b7db802716615d (Security: CVE-2026-14676, in tag REL_18_6 and not in REL_18_4), which replaces the fixed-size buffer for the normalized query in contrib/pg_stat_statements/pg_stat_statements.c with an expansible StringInfo; it is the only change to that file between those tags. PostgreSQL 18.5 was never released (the 18.6 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.6/, say so), so although Alpine's security database lists this CVE for postgresql18 under 18.5-r0, this owner has no 18.5-r0 build and its first build that carries the fix is 18.6-r0. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built with Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD from the 3.23-stable branch of aports (current revision https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD) and the upstream PostgreSQL source release of the same version; none of the patches that APKBUILD applies, at any revision used for these builds, changes the files this fix changes. As of 2026-11-28 the DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository publishes builds of source postgresql18 at 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0, for x86_64 and aarch64. We read every one of them on both architectures, with package checksums verified against the repository index, and in each the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql18/postgres, reports the PostgreSQL release matching its package version. pg_stat_statements.so ships in the postgresql18-contrib package of every one of those builds on both architectures. In its dynamic symbol table, the 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0 builds import the StringInfo functions appendStringInfo, appendBinaryStringInfo and initStringInfoExt and no longer import pg_sprintf, while the earlier builds import pg_sprintf and none of those three, on both architectures; the module's source at the REL_18_4 tag uses no StringInfo. 18.6-r0 is the first published build for Alpine 3.23 that carries the fix, and 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0 carry it. The earlier published builds (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0 and 18.4-r0) are built from PostgreSQL releases before the fix and are affected.
